column3: “Struck Ziklag” is rendered “overthrown Ziklag.”
NASB supplies “and all,” and “not they had killed anyone” becomes “without killing anyone.”
Close to the Hebrew.

“The wife of Nabal” is rendered “the widow of Nabal.”
“Said to stone him” is rendered “spoke of stoning him,” and “bitter of soul” as “embittered.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Marauding band” is rendered “band,” and NASB supplies “all” after “rescue.”
“Wadi” is rendered “brook.”
NASB adds “for,” giving the reason, and moves “remained behind” to the end.
“In the open country” is rendered “in the field.”
“His spirit returned to him” is rendered “his spirit revived”; “food” is rendered “bread.”
“If I was sick today three” is rendered “when I fell sick three days ago.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The oath formula “if you will kill me” is rendered “that you will not kill me.”
“Celebrating” is rendered “dancing,” and “in all the plunder” as “because of all the great spoil.”
“Struck them down” is rendered “slaughtered them.”
“Rescued” is rendered “recovered,” and “Amalek” as “the Amalekites.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew is difficult (“they drove before that livestock”); NASB renders “which the people drove ahead of the other livestock.” The meaning is uncertain.
“Asked them about welfare” is rendered “greeted them.”
“Every man evil and worthlessness” is rendered “all the wicked and worthless men.” The Hebrew “with me” is rendered “with us.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “who.”

“A blessing” is rendered “a gift,” and “his friend” as “his friends.”
